sources.title: J. Sirker, Transport in one-dimensional integrable quantum systems, SciPost Physics Lecture Notes 17 (2020), full 19-page lecture notes

contents.name: §2, equations (2.1)–(2.2): local continuity equation and spin current orientation
contents.support: Supports the lattice bond-current orientation and commutator convention in the XXZ spin chain. The local general-charge identity is proved completely in lem-qsmx-lattice-current-continuity.

contents.name: §2.1, equations (2.9)–(2.14): finite-system Mazur projection bound
contents.support: Supports the finite Cesàro current-correlation and conserved-overlap context. The authored proof gives the general Gram-matrix form and retains degenerate energy blocks without importing a thermodynamic-limit step.

contents.name: §2.2, equations (2.23)–(2.28): Drude part versus a regular integrable correlation
contents.support: The source's XXZ transport discussion motivates the distinction between persistent and decaying correlations. Its model-specific conductivity formulas are not imported; the authored claim assumes absolute integrability and proves only the variance-growth identity.

contents.name: General local charge continuity and open-boundary cancellation
contents.support: Sirker gives the spin-chain continuity/current convention in §2, equations (2.1)–(2.2). The local proof extends the sign calculation to the stated finite open or periodic nearest-neighbor data and proves endpoint cancellation directly.

contents.name: Equations (3.1)–(3.8): displacement variance and equilibrium velocity autocorrelation
contents.support: Supports the classical stationary-correlation interpretation. The source is limited to fluid self-diffusion in the linear-response regime; the authored theorem states a mathematical covariance identity and does not infer a physical diffusion law.
